title: How Marc Lou validates a startup idea: painkiller, personal use, launch in weeks
summary: Marc shares a 3-step framework for picking which startup to build: choose painkillers over vitamins, build things you would really use, and ditch ideas that take longer than a month. He backs it with examples from his own products like Habits Garden, VirallyBot and WorkbookPDF.

principles.text: Build painkillers, not vitamins. People pay far more readily for products that solve real problems.
principles.quote: People are much more willing to pay for a product that solves their problems.

principles.text: Turn a vitamin into a painkiller by explaining why it is a must-have for the user.
principles.quote: Turn vitamins into painkillers by explaining why your product is a must-have: Track your habits → Diet habit you won’t quit

principles.text: Keyword research validates demand, but actually using the product yourself matters far more.
principles.quote: Validating ideas (i.e. keyword research) is important. But it’s pale in comparison to actually using the product yourself

principles.text: Using your own product gives you the frustration insight needed to write on-point copy and pick features.
principles.quote: You understand the frustration, your copy will be on point

principles.text: Ditch ideas that take longer than a month to build; estimates always run long and risk burnout.
principles.quote: If it takes 6 months to build a startup, it’s not a good idea. It will actually take 12 months (overthinking and bugs) and you could burn out and quit.

principles.text: Cut time-to-market by preselling, skipping nonessentials, and shrinking ideas to one feature.
principles.quote: Presell a product. Ditch code testing & dark mode. Break big ideas into 1-feature-only products
